ruling.recommended_action: Route to a Ryde human safety reviewer: read chat #1 and #2 (F3, F4) in full context, obtain the driver's account of events, and decide whether the driver's message and conduct amount to intimidation/abuse or a safety-code breach before any fare or account decision is made.
ruling.reasoning:
This case is filed as a safety incident, and the chat record contains a rider request to leave and a driver reply that reads, in context, as a threat to lock the rider in the car [F3][F4]. Under SAFE-1, threats and intimidation aimed at the other party are not subject to automated ruling and must go to a human reviewer with a factual summary [SAFE-1]. The trace confirms the safety screen passed and that escalate is the only permitted outcome here [F5][SAFE-1], so I do not rule on the fare.

What happened: the trip ran Clarke Quay → Bedok Mall on 17:08–17:31, 15.4 km actual versus 15.5 km optimal and 23.7 min versus 21.8 min estimated — i.e. no measurable route deviation, the distance was actually 0.1 km shorter than optimal [F1][F2]. At 17:09 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here," and at 17:10 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F3][F4]. The driver's post-trip statement says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and he told her to sit down "for her own safety" and drove on [F6]. Both messages are timestamped and the chat record is complete, so timing is not the problem [F5]; the undecided element is what the driver's words and conduct mean and whether they are a safety-code breach [F4][F6].

For the reviewer: the driver's message on its face conditions a confinement-like action ("I lock the doors") on the rider's compliance, and the rider says she felt unsafe for the whole ride; the driver frames the same words as a safety instruction during a moving-car door-opening incident [F4][F6]. The reviewer should check whether the driver was told to stop and refused to let the rider exit, whether the doors were in fact locked, and whether the whole ride continued against the rider's stated wish; SAFE-1 bars "threats and intimidation" and abuse of any kind, and the code of conduct requires drivers not to take matters into their own hands [SAFE-1]. No account action is taken here; the structured flag is left false, and SAFE-1 does not itself call for one [SAFE-1].

Because the safety screen decides the outcome, the route/fare elements need no finding: with F1 showing no excess distance, any deviation claim would fail on the record [F1][RD-1], and the profile facts (rider and driver with no prior disputes or upheld cases) cannot decide anything on their own [F7][F8][RD-6]. Evidence is sufficient for the escalation itself — the chat is complete and timed [F5] — but the meaning of the driver's words is reserved to the human reviewer, not to an automated ruling.
